title: Midpoint predictors kept abundance-change correlation signs in six bird drought samples from a 2024 release
abstract: We tested whether changing the abundance predictor changes the sign of its link to absolute drought change. We used 106 records in six samples from four studies in a 2024 bird drought release. All six Pearson correlation signs persisted when the predictor changed from reference abundance to the two-condition midpoint. Four signs were negative and two were positive. Three negative samples kept their signs after each one-species omission with both predictors. Exact covariance identities show that the midpoint sign measures a change in observed across-species abundance variance. It does not identify a biological mechanism or remove detection bias. Three Hawaiian samples share species and controls. Different methods, selected species, publication bias, incomplete survey information and small samples limit inference. No pollution effect or causal climate-change effect was tested. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and a figure are included. External source records remain outside the package.
